results.summary: bfCPU implements a universal Turing machine as a superset of the Brainf*ck language. It is a 2x2 tile SystemVerilog design clocked at 10 MHz, with UART for serial communication and QSPI pins for memory access. The design is intended to be programmed and controlled via UART, though specific usage details are not provided. Documentation is limited to the title and pin names, so the exact instruction set and operation are not fully described.

This design is an 8-wire DC continuity tester for Ethernet cables, driving each wire in turn and reporting per-wire pass/fail on eight LEDs. It requires a far-end shorting plug that ties all wires together and a near-end board with series resistors, pull-downs, and TVS diodes for protection. The chip continuously retests, allowing intermittent faults to be observed as flickering LEDs. It is a practical test tool rather than a data communication device, and its operation is well documented.

The IEEE Bubble Sort Engine is a hardware implementation of the bubble sort algorithm, accepting an 8-bit data stream and outputting sorted data. It uses a ready/valid handshake protocol with start, in_valid, in_last, out_ready, out_valid, and out_last signals. The design is a 1x1 tile with no external hardware required, as stated in the documentation. However, the documentation is minimal, providing only pin names and a brief description, so details of the sorting process and performance are not available.

TTSKY-SPSRAM-direct is a single-port SRAM block with 128 words of 8 bits, directly connected to the Tiny Tapeout tile pins. It provides address, write enable, data input, and data output signals, and performs read or write operations on each clock edge. The design is full custom and operates at 66 MHz, allowing it to be used as a standalone memory block. Testing involves writing data to an address and reading it back to verify functionality.

Tiny Canvas is a hardware drawing tool that mimics MS Paint, controlled by an SNES-compatible gamepad and outputting canvas coordinates and color data over I2C. It supports RGB color mixing, variable brush sizes, symmetry modes, and fill rectangle operations. The design requires a Gamepad PMOD and an SNES controller, and an I2C master device to render the canvas on a display. It is a 1x1 tile design that streams paint events in real-time to a host for a 256x256 canvas.

TinyCore8 is an 8-bit programmable CPU with eight registers, a 4-bit program counter, and a simple accumulator-style instruction set. Programs are loaded serially through dedicated pins, and execution starts when the run signal is asserted. The CPU can perform ALU operations, branches, and I/O with a 4-bit input and 8-bit output. A smoke-test program is provided to demonstrate basic functionality.

This project implements a Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) signal detection engine that processes a 14-bit ADC input and displays detection results on a 7-segment display. It uses an IIR running average to estimate the noise threshold and compares the input signal against a scaled threshold to detect targets. The design requires an external 14-bit signal source and a 7-segment display for visual feedback. It is a simplified version without a buzzer, optimized for area-constrained silicon.

Sky26a Advanced TRNG is a true random number generator based on an 8-oscillator ring oscillator bank, with NIST health monitors and six chaotic whiteners. It provides random bytes via parallel output, UART, and SPI interfaces, and includes enable, auto mode, and tunable select pins. The design is a 2x2 tile and requires no external hardware beyond a standard Tiny Tapeout carrier board. It is intended for research-grade randomness generation with comprehensive characterization features.

Tiny Secure Telemetry Engine is an 8-bit security and integrity co-processor that supports nonlinear permutation, keystream generation, and CRC modes. It mixes input data with internal state using nibble substitution, bit rotations, and XOR diffusion, with mode pins selecting the operation. The design is a 1x1 tile with an 8-bit input and output, and no external hardware is specified. Documentation is brief, so the exact cryptographic strength and intended use cases are not fully detailed.

Hey FlexCompute-130 is a hybrid accelerator combining an INT8 neural processing unit (NPU) and a 12-bit CORDIC processor for functions like SINH, COSH, and ATAN. It accepts 8-bit data input and provides an 8-bit accumulator output, with SPI for weight loading and mode pins to select between NPU and CORDIC operation. The design is a 1x1 tile and requires external SPI master for configuration. Documentation is limited to a brief description and pin names, so detailed operation and performance are not fully described.
